messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: spike in 5xx and gateway timeouts on dedicated-cluster-delta affecting tenant OrbitAI. error-rate 5xx > 8% over 5m, p95 latency increased to 3.4s, KV eviction rate elevated. paging oncall.
pagerduty: Paging oncall-sre (primary) — incident triggered by infra/alerts/dedicated/5xx-elevated. priority=P1.
oncall-sre: ack'd. joining now. can someone paste the tenant and pool ids?
Jordan H: OrbitAI, pool delta-gpu-7, fleet-id fk-3487. seeing heavy seq-len 2048 tails. logs show repeated kv cache misses + OOMs on a few allocs.
Priya K: I see the same — gateway logs show 502s with 'backend-reset' and timeouts from qproxy. Kibana: https://kibana/redwood/d/xyz (short link)
Samir A: stack traces indicate a sustained large-batch training job in tenant OrbitAI that spiked GPU mem usage. noisy-neighbor hypothesis.
Lee T: current capacity util across delta-gpu-7: GPU mem 94% avg, NVLINK queues saturated on 3 nodes, inflight queue lengths > 120. shedding policies aren't firing due to reserved capacity flag for OrbitAI.
Marta S: Customer impact: OrbitAI reports degraded realtime completions and increased retry/error rates. Support ticket #ORD-8123 opened, customer on standby for first update.
oncall-sre: immediate mitigations: 1) throttle OrbitAI to 50% of normal TPS via rate-limiter override 2) enable eviction for large-batch jobs on pool delta-gpu-7 3) failover traffic to dedicated-cluster-epsilon for non-sensitive requests. executing now.
Jordan H: running command to set tenant throttle:
```
redwoodctl tenants update --tenant orbitai --rate-limit 50%
```
Priya K: throttle applied, traffic dropped ~46% within 30s. 5xx rate decreased from 8.2% -> 3.1% in 2m. p95 down to 1.2s.
Samir A: enabling eviction policy for big-batch annotations on nodes: patch applied to autoscaler config. will induce job preemption for jobs > 12GB ephemeral cache.
Lee T: failover route prep: adding fallback to dedicated-cluster-epsilon for model endpoints where model pinning allows variant fallback. updating routing table.
Marta S: Sent initial customer update: "we're investigating elevated errors and have throttled traffic to stabilize. We will follow up with postmortem." Customer asked for ETA. suggested 1h for stabilization, will propose permanent mitigation.
oncall-sre: Observability: KV eviction metrics show a sharp drop after throttle, but 3 nodes still show high IO. scheduling controlled drain of two noisy nodes for memory reclamation. will cordon and redeploy.
Jordan H: cordon started on node delta-7b3, redeploying runtime. logs:
```
[delta-7b3] evicting KV: 24k entries
runtime: gc triggered, freed 11.3GB
```
Priya K: after node drain p95 latency stabilized under 800ms for 80% of traffic. remaining 5xx are mostly gateway timeouts for X-large generation requests pinned to OrbitAI's reserved instances.
Samir A: root cause summary draft: OrbitAI kicked off a large-sweep generation job with long sequences and unusually high batch sizes; combined with reserved capacity and lack of per-tenant memory caps this pushed a few hosts to KV pressure and runtime OOM, leading to 502s. mitigation: per-tenant memory quota + soft eviction + better noisy-tenant detection.
oncall-sre: Next steps: 1) keep throttle at 50% for 30m and monitor 2) patch autoscaler to enforce per-tenant mem caps (hotfix roll planned in 2h) 3) follow-up customer comms and postmortem. assign owners: Priya for steady-state metrics, Jordan for node redeploys, Samir for autoscaler patch, Marta for customer comms.
Marta S: I'll send the next update to OrbitAI: stabilization in progress, patch ETA 2h, will provide postmortem within 48h. ticket updated.
Lee T: creating incident task in JIRA: INF-71290, tagging 'noisy-tenant' 'dedicated' 'kv-eviction'.
oncall-sre: closing active paging for now — we will keep this thread live for coordination. if error-rate goes above 5% re-open paging. thanks all :thumbsup:
